battle.name: 郭方預起義
battle.brief: 大業九年（613），隋煬帝第二次征高句麗、括戶徵兵之際，河北南部鄴郡一帶州郡皆生民變，郡人郭方預聚眾起兵，轉掠縣邑，隋廷遣郡兵與將領追討平之。此役僅存編年殘卷，戰鬥經過無考。卡面埃及長矛屬早王朝青銅兵器，與此役毫無干涉；場內對應的是隋軍步卒長矛與騎兵馬槊。

kit.name: 埃及長矛
kit.history: 早王朝時期的長矛，銅或青銅矛頭綁在木杆上。埃及人用它守城垣，後來也用它收復失地。

countries: 交戰雙方是隋朝中央與州縣軍政體系一方，和由郭方預領起、隨後捲入河北、山東、河南一線州郡的起義群眾一方。隋朝這邊的兵力並非單一常備軍：河北、山東所調用的是郡兵與縣兵，多由免役戶與鄉里百姓按戶抽丁組成，戰時披甲執矛，戰罷歸農；真正有作戰經驗的是自高句麗前線調回的宿將與臨時徵募的驍騎，其中張須陀一路的精騎最為著名，樊子蓋則奉詔往山東、河南一帶捕集逃戶、討平群賊。指揮系統上，煬帝以詔令直接調度各道行軍與各州郡兵，郡太守、縣令自將城守，遇賊則閉城固守、發丁出戰，同時向州與中央請兵。起義一方則是州郡內部的逃亡戶、逃兵、匠役、僧道與失業農夫按鄉里關係結成的武裝，首領多為郡縣中的吏卒、豪右或亡命之徒，郭方預即屬此類；各部名號互不統一，號令各自，器械多靠自備，因水旱與兵禍聚集，起事後一面攻掠郡縣、一面靠劫糧與裹挾維持。由於兩邊都缺乏穩定後勤，這類起義的生死幾乎全看能不能搶在官軍集結之前站住州城、撐過第一批援軍。
countriesEn: The two sides were the Sui court with its state and county military apparatus on one hand, and on the other the insurgents led by Guo Fangyu, who drew the counties of Hebei, Shandong and Henan into the disturbance. The Sui strength was not a single standing army. The troops raised in Hebei and Shandong were commandery and county levies, enlisted from exempt households and village peasants by household quota, armed and drilled while the campaign lasted and returning to the fields afterwards. The soldiers who actually carried experience were the veterans pulled back from the Goguryeo front together with hastily recruited cavalry, above all the mounted troopers of Zhang Xuotuo, while Fan Zigae was sent to the eastern districts to round up absentees and suppress bands. Command ran on the emperor's own edicts, dispatching field armies and county levies through the circuits; commandery governors and county magistrates held their walled towns, kept the gates shut when raiders came, mustered the local men to fight, and petitioned the prefecture and the court for troops. The insurgents were fugitives from the household registers, deserters, craftsmen, monks and unemployed peasants banded together through village ties, and their leaders were usually local clerks, minor landowners or men already in flight; Guo Fangyu was one of these. The bands had no common name and no uniform command, each keeping its own banner and raising its own gear, and they survived by seizing grain and carrying the population off with them. With no stable supply on either side, the life or death of a rising like this usually came down to whether it could seize a prefectural city before the imperial troops closed in, and whether it could hold out past the first wave of relief.
people: 這場起義唯一留下姓名的首領就是郭方預。《隋書·煬帝紀》在編排大業九年州郡事變時，把「郭方預」三字列在起義名錄中，卻沒有記下他的籍貫、出身、起兵的地點與年月，也沒有留下他本人的結局；《資治通鑑》卷一百八十二沿用同一份名錄，只在字句間提示大業九年天下群盜蜂起。同卷並列的名字還有竇建德、張金稱、孫安祖、高士達、劉霸道、孟海公、王薄、杜彥冰、宋子賢、李德逸、白瑜娑、孟讓、郝孝德、格謙、陳瑱、梁慧尚、李三兒、朱燮、管崇、呂明星、向海明、劉元進等，各自據一州一郡起事，彼此並無統屬。隋廷方面的關鍵人物是煬帝本人：第二次征高句麗的隊伍還壓在遼東與涿郡一線，他只能在州縣之間分遣將領應變，皇太子兼尚書令楊廣分掌中樞，河北方向的追討主要落在張須陀身上，樊子蓋則在河南、山東整頓戶籍、追捕亡命。九月在黎陽起兵的楊玄感是同年最著名的一次反亂，他是楊素長子、與煬帝同族，起事後聚眾約八萬，兵敗時部眾潰散，牽動了河北一線的官軍調度，也讓郭方預一類州郡起義有了可指望的響應對象。
peopleEn: Guo Fangyu is the only leader of this rising whose name has survived. When the Annals of Emperor Yang of the Sui arrange the disturbances of the ninth year of Daye, they set the three characters Guo Fangyu down in a roster of rebellions, yet record neither his native place, nor his background, nor the place and month in which he raised his banner, nor how his life ended. The Zizhi Tongjian, in volume 182, reuses that same roster and only hints, in the turn of its sentences, that in that year rebels rose in every direction. Names listed beside his include Dou Jiande, Zhang Jincheng, Sun Anzu, Gao Shida, Liu Badao, Meng Haigong, Wang Bo, Du Yanbing, Song Zixian, Li Deyi, Bai Yusuo, Meng Rang, Hao Xiaode, Ge Qian, Chen Zhen, Liang Huishang, Li San'er, Zhu Xie, Guan Chong, Lü Mingxing, Xiang Haiming and Liu Yuanjin, each holding one prefecture or county, none subordinate to another. On the court side the decisive figure was the emperor himself: with the second Goguryeo campaign still pinning the army in Liaodong and Zhuojun, he could only dispatch commanders piecemeal to the affected districts, while the crown prince and minister-in-chief Yang Guang handled the central government, the pursuit in Hebei fell mainly to Zhang Xuotuo, and Fan Zigae reorganised the registers and hunted absentees in Henan and Shandong. The best known rising of that year was Yang Xiangan's at Liyang in the ninth month: eldest son of Yang Su and a kinsman of the emperor, he gathered about eighty thousand men and was defeated, the dispersal of his host disturbing the imperial disposition in Hebei and giving risings of Guo Fangyu's kind an object to rally around.
kits: 起義本身幾乎沒有留下裝備記載，只能從當年隋軍的編制與同一批起義者的常見配備推知。隋軍這邊，步兵骨幹是長矛與槊：矛為步卒基本兵器，用於結陣拒馬與守城垣，槊則分步槊與馬槊，馬槊是騎兵對騎兵、對車陣的衝擊兵器，兩者都需要相當的握力與槓桿，士卒多在郡兵中自備木杆。刀劍方面是環首刀與陌刀，陌刀為禁軍裝備，用於破騎兵與砍斷拒馬；弓弩以角筋複合弓與蹶張弩、機弩、床弩為主，弩用於守城與壓制城頭守軍，床弩一發可以重箭破門。防具方面有札甲、鐵鍔與盾，騎兵另有頸甲與馬鎧。攻城與野戰的輔助器械有撞車、雲梯、櫓、拒馬與鹿角，並使用火矢與猛火油對付城牆與船隊，糧食則依賴江南運河轉輸的粟米，濟南、彭城一線多屯糧。起義者一端的武器以自備與徵集為主，常見的是竹木削成的槊、柴刀改成的長刀、戈、獵弓，以及耒耜一類農具削尖充作刺兵器；鄉里出身的射手多仍在用較早的角弓，起義初期甚少鐵甲。卡面那件埃及長矛屬於早王朝的銅與青銅矛具，綁在木杆上用於守城與收復失地，與隋代鐵矛並不同源，但它確實說明了長矛作為冷兵器時代步兵基本器物的位置：六百年後的中原，矛仍是城牆上拒敵的第一線器械。
kitsEn: The rising itself leaves no record of its equipment, so the arms of the insurgents can only be inferred from the Sui order of battle and from what such bands are known to carry. In the imperial camp the backbone of the infantry was the spear and the shao: the spear was the basic arm of the foot soldier, used to form a bristling line against cavalry and to hold ramparts, while the shao existed in a foot and a mounted form, the mounted shao being the arm a horseman used against cavalry and against war-wagon lines, and both demanded a great deal of grip and leverage, the shaft usually being the soldier's own wood. The blades were the ring-pommel dao and the modao, the latter an arm of the palace guards used to break cavalry and cut down cheval-de-frise; the bows and crossbows were the composite bow of horn and sinew, the strong-pull crossbow, the light crossbow and the bed crossbow, the crossbows serving to hold walls and to sweep the ramparts, and the bed crossbow sending a single heavy bolt through a gate. The armour was lamellar plate, iron helms and shields, the cavalry adding neck guards and horse armour. Field and siege adjuncts included battering rams, scaling ladders, movable shields, caltrops and antler-shaped obstacles, and the Sui used fire arrows and naphtha against walls and ships, while the commissary depended on millet ferried from Jiangnan up the canal, with depots in the Jinan and Pengcheng districts. On the insurgent side the weapons were self-provided or simply picked up: bamboo and wooden shao, long knives reworked from billhooks, the ge, hunting bows, and farming implements sharpened into stabbing weapons; archers from the villages still used older horn bows, and iron armour was scarce in the first months. The Egyptian spear on the card belongs to the copper and bronze arm of the early dynastic period, lashed to a wooden shaft for wall defence and for the recovery of lost ground; it is not related to the iron spears of the Sui, but it does show where the spear stood among the cold weapons of the age. Six centuries later on the Central Plain, the spear was still the first line of defence along a city wall.
tactics: 州郡起義的戰術基因是不據城、不結陣、不與官軍主力決戰。郭方預這類首領手上的部眾，多數只有鄉里同鄉的關係網，缺乏軍紀與攻城器械，因此最常見的打法是先以小股人馬在州城之外的鄉里活動，避開郡兵主力，等守軍出城或調往別處，再合擊縣邑、截斷糧道；奪得倉廩之後，把糧食分給部眾，趁煬帝的遠征部隊還在遼東、山東與河南的郡兵主力被迫分兵追討的時間窗口擴張。一旦官軍騎兵到達，起義軍便放棄城池，退入鄉里、山澤與水網地帶，利用地形切割追兵縱隊，再於夜間或雨霧中襲擊糧隊與傳令兵。攻城的手段以突門、攀牆與火攻為主，使用的多是臨時器械：拆除民舍取梁木作撞杆、用浸油麻布焚燒城門、拆屋瓦投擲守軍。官軍這邊的戰術則相對規整：郡兵據城固守、倚城垣以長矛與弩箭抵擋，州與中央則調集精騎作追討，追討的關鍵是斷糧道而非正面合戰，張須陀在河北山東的戰術正是以精騎先擊其部眾再追奔潰散之師，迫敵在道路上疲於奔命，同時修築營柵、絕其汲道與糧道。樊子蓋在河南山東的做法更偏重登記戶口、封鎖道路、據險設柵，讓起義者得不到食宿與補充。一場這樣的衝突通常沒有會戰名份，勝負在數日內以城破、眾散或首領被擒告終。
tacticsEn: The tactical make-up of a county rising was: do not hold a city, do not form up in ranks, do not meet the imperial main force in battle. The followers of a leader like Guo Fangyu were bound together only by village acquaintance and lacked drill and siege equipment, so the usual method was to move in small parties outside the prefectural city, avoid the county levies, and wait for the garrison to march out or be drawn off, then strike the smaller county seats together and cut the supply road. Once the granaries were taken, the grain was shared among the band, and the rising grew in the window in which the emperor's expeditionary force was still in Liaodong and the levies of Shandong and Henan had to be split three ways. Once imperial cavalry arrived, the insurgents would leave the towns, fall back into the countryside, the hills and the marsh country, use the ground to cut the columns of pursuit, and raid baggage trains and couriers by night or in rain and mist. Towns were taken by surprising the gate, scaling the wall and by fire, with improvised means: beams pulled out of houses to serve as rams, oil-soaked sacking set against the gates, roof tiles thrown down on the defenders. On the imperial side the method was more regular. County levies held the walls and met the enemy with long spears and crossbow bolts from behind the rampart; the prefecture and the court concentrated picked cavalry for the pursuit, and the key was to cut the grain road rather than to win a set-piece battle. In Hebei and Shandong the method of Zhang Xuotuo was to strike the mass of the insurgents with cavalry first and then chase the broken host into the roads, wearing them out on the march, while building fortified camps and closing their springs and their grain roads. The approach of Fan Zigae in Henan and Shandong leaned on registering households, sealing the roads and holding the passes with palisades, so that the insurgents could find neither food nor shelter. A conflict of this kind usually had no battle to be named; it was settled within days by the fall of a town, the dispersal of a band, or the capture of a leader.
data: 可核的數字多來自編年史對大業九年整體局勢的記載，而非這場起義本身。兵員方面，《資治通鑑》記隋軍第二次征高句麗渡遼之師號一百一十三萬五千人，而糧運不繼，至遼東時士卒死者過半，這一支出遠的隊伍正是同年州郡無力鎮壓的根源。州郡起義的規模，多半從眾數萬到眾數十萬不等：張金稱在鄴郡聚眾號稱百萬，竇建德在河北眾至數十萬，楊玄感九月在黎陽起兵則聚眾約八萬；相較之下，載於編年的單郡起義如郭方預一類，人數當在數千至數萬之譜，但史無明文，故只作此推斷。饑荒方面，《隋書》記大業九年江南、江淮大水，河北、河南亦乏食，郡縣饑民相食的記載屢見；同年二月朝廷下詔括天下漏丁，把逃戶、匿丁與度人為僧道者一律重新登記以充軍實與租調，民間因被追捕而群起者眾。戰果方面，《資治通鑑》記張須陀破高士達，斬首萬餘級、俘虜數萬，張金稱最盛時眾號百萬，後為官軍所破，首級傳送長安。距離與時間上，鄴郡距京師洛陽約六百里，郡兵自州城調至縣邑多需數日，山東、河北一線的郡兵無法在數日之內集中到同一方向，這正是起義得以蔓延的實際原因。
dataEn: The figures that can be checked come mostly from the annalistic record of the general situation in the ninth year of Daye, and not from this rising itself. On numbers of troops, the Zizhi Tongjian records that in the second campaign against Goguryeo the Sui army crossing to Liaodong was numbered at one million one hundred and thirty-five thousand men, and that because supply did not keep up, more than half of the soldiers were dead by the time they reached Liaodong; that distant army was the root of the counties' inability to hold down disorder in the same year. The size of the county risings ran from several tens of thousands to hundreds of thousands: Zhang Jincheng gathered a following numbered at a hundred thousand in the Ye prefecture, Dou Jiande's numbers in Hebei reached tens of thousands, and Yang Xiangan, rising at Liyang in the ninth month, assembled about eighty thousand. By comparison, a single county rising such as Guo Fangyu's must have numbered from a few thousand to a few tens of thousands, but no text says so, and this is therefore an inference. On famine, the History of Sui records great floods in Jiangnan and the Jiang-Huai in the ninth year of Daye, and scarcity in Hebei and Henan, with the starving of the population appearing again and again in the local gazetteers; in the second month of the same year the court ordered a general registration of all hidden persons, so that absentees, concealed households and those who had taken monastic vows might be entered anew as liable for service and for tax, and the manhunt that followed drove villages into open revolt. On results, the Zizhi Tongjian has Zhang Xuotuo breaking Gao Shida, with more than ten thousand heads taken and tens of thousands captured, and Zhang Jincheng, whose following was given as a hundred thousand at its height, was later broken and his head sent to Chang'an. On distance and time, the Ye prefecture lay some six hundred li from the capital of Luoyang, county levies needed several days to move from the prefectural seat down to the county seats, and the levies of Shandong and Hebei could not be brought together in the same direction within a few days, which is the practical reason the risings were able to spread.
cause: 起義的直接起因是國家把戰爭與財政的雙重壓力同時壓到州縣百姓頭上。大業九年二月，朝廷下詔括天下漏丁，把逃戶、匿丁與度人為僧道者一律重新登記為丁，任何人不得隱匿，這道詔令在饑荒最嚴重的年份徵發最狠，州縣官吏為完成額外多出的丁口與賦稅，四處追捕人戶，於是鄉里之間互相舉發，民間怨憤集中爆發。背景則是第二次征高句麗：隋軍傾國力遠征，糧食主要由江南經運河轉輸，一旦江淮水災沖毀漕渠與堤壩，遠征軍的給養便無以為繼，前線吃緊、州郡空虛兩件事同時發生。饑荒把大量農民推離土地，流民由淮、泗入荊襄、入河北，郡縣的常備力量不足以攔截，遇到有能號召的首領便聚集成眾。既有矛盾之外，隋朝以《開皇律》立下的嚴刑峻法在地方上並未真正落到實處，郡吏對逃亡戶的催逼與富豪的兼併土地又常常越過律令的界線，於是起義最初往往不是有綱領的反抗，而是一批人趁著官軍不在本地、無人可問的時候，把鬱積多年的不滿變成一次集體的武裝行動，一旦成功便有更多人跟隨，失敗便各自散去。
causeEn: The immediate cause was that the state pressed the cost of war and the cost of taxation onto the population of the counties at the same time. In the second month of the ninth year of Daye the court ordered a general registration of all hidden persons, so that absentees, concealed households and those who had taken monastic vows were entered again as taxable and liable for service, and no one was allowed to hide. This edict came in the hungriest of years and demanded the heaviest levies, and the county officials, pressed to produce extra labour and extra revenue, hunted people from house to house, so that villages turned informer on one another and the accumulated resentment of the people came out in a single burst. Behind it lay the second Goguryeo campaign: the Sui had emptied the country into that expedition, and its grain came chiefly from Jiangnan by canal, so once the floods in the Jiang-Huai broke the embankments and the canal, the distant army had no supply; the front was short of food and the counties were empty at the same time. The famine pushed great numbers of farmers off their land, and the moving people came from Huai and Si into Jing and Xiang and into Hebei, where the county forces could not intercept them; meeting a leader able to call them, they massed into a band. On top of the older grievances, the strict penal code of the Kaihuang statutes had never really been enforced locally, and the pursuit of absentees by county clerks and the annexation of land by the powerful frequently went beyond what the statutes allowed. A rebellion was therefore often not a movement with a programme at all, but a body of people who, finding the imperial soldiers away from home and no one to answer to, turned long-suppressed resentment into one collective act of arms; once it succeeded others followed, and once it failed they dispersed.
impact: 單就郭方預這一場起義而言，史料只留下姓名，它帶來的直接改變有限：郡內的統治秩序被破壞了數月，戶口重新編排，鄉里的生產與徵發中斷，之後仍回到郡兵與州府的管治之下。但放在大業九年整體看，這類州郡起義構成了一條清晰的連鎖：它們把隋朝最後的財政與兵源基礎，也就是編戶齊民與租調力役，從內部挖空，使朝廷對地方的抽汲愈來愈急，而地方愈來愈不能提供，兩者互為因果。到大業十年之後，河北與山東的郡縣已多為竇建德、劉黑闕、王世充等武裝所據，隋朝在名義上還有天下，實際上能調動的郡兵所剩無幾；江淮的劉元進、浙西的陳瑱等也讓東南無法成為朝廷的糧倉。歷史的另一個作用是示範：起義者用最原始的鄉里武裝證明了只要官軍主力被牽制在外，州城是可以被拿下的，這正是後來瓦崗軍在黎陽倉、李密在洛陽以及竇建德稱夏王時所依循的同一條戰略邏輯。對後世史書編纂而言，有姓名而無事跡本身也是一種記錄：唐初修《隋書》，把關於小股起義的零星材料收進帝紀的編年目錄，卻不為他們立傳，使得這批人在文獻中的存在感遠低於其當時的破壞力。
impactEn: By itself, the rising of Guo Fangyu left little beyond a name. The order of a county was broken for some months, households were re-registered, the production and the levies of the villages were interrupted, and then everything went back under the county levies and the prefectural government. Set within the ninth year of Daye as a whole, however, these county risings formed a clear chain. They hollowed out from within the last financial and manpower base of the Sui, the registered taxed households and the rent and labour services, so that the extraction by the court grew ever heavier while the localities grew ever less able to provide, each feeding the other. After the tenth year of Daye, the commanderies and counties of Hebei and Shandong were mostly in the hands of armed bands such as Dou Jiande, Liu Hei and Wang Shichong; the Sui still claimed the empire on paper while the county levies it could actually move were almost gone, and the risings of Liu Yuanjin in the Jiang-Huai and of Chen Zhen in Zhexi meant the southeast could no longer serve as the court's granary. A second effect was demonstration. Armed bands built on the simplest village loyalties proved that, as long as the imperial main force was tied down elsewhere, a prefectural city could be taken, and that is the same strategic logic followed later by the Wagang host at the Liyang granary, by Li Mi at Luoyang and by Dou Jiande when he proclaimed himself king of Xia. For the writing of later history, the very fact that a name survives without a career is itself a kind of record: when the Tang compiled the History of Sui, the scattered materials on these small risings went into the annalistic roster of the emperor's reign and no biography was written for them, so that their presence in the written record is far smaller than the disruption they actually caused.
result: 結局是這場起義沒有發展成可以自立的力量，也沒有留下可供追認的戰役記錄。官軍這邊的處置方式與同年其他州郡起義相同：郡兵與募兵先封守住縣境要道，調回前線的宿將率精騎入境，以追討潰散之師的方式迫使起義者分散，郭方預的部眾在失去郡城、糧食與同鄉網絡之後各自散去，其中一部分併入竇建德、張金稱、王薄等較大的武裝，成為大業十年前後河北與山東義軍的人力來源；首領郭方預本人的下落，編年史並無記載，後世也沒有留下任何傳記，這正是隋末數百名起義首領中相當一部分的共同命運。從全局看，大業九年爆發的起義潮在兩年內被隋廷以郡兵、募兵與鎮守重鎮的策略壓下去，但每一次鎮壓都消耗掉一批可用之兵與一筆可收之賦，而新的一次叛亂總在別的州郡重新冒出來，隋朝的崩解因此不是被某一次戰役決定，而是被這條不斷重複的循環耗盡。三年之後，大業十三年（617）太原留守李淵起兵；再一年，隋煬帝在江都遇弒，隋朝覆亡，唐朝接手的地方秩序，是在這批起義已經把郡縣系統打散之後重新拼起來的。
resultEn: The outcome was that the rising never became a power able to stand on its own, and it left no battle record to be commemorated. On the imperial side the treatment was the same as for the other county risings of that year: county levies and recruited men first sealed the roads into the county, and veterans brought back from the front entered the district with cavalry, pursuing the broken host in order to scatter it. Guo Fangyu's followers, once they had lost the county town, the grain and the network of village acquaintance, dispersed, and part of them was absorbed into the larger hosts of Dou Jiande, Zhang Jincheng and Wang Bo, becoming manpower for the insurgents of Hebei and Shandong around the tenth year of Daye. The fate of Guo Fangyu himself is not recorded in the annals, and no biography of him survives, which was the common lot of a good many hundreds of rebel leaders at the end of the Sui. Across the whole picture, the wave of risings that broke out in the ninth year of Daye was put down within two years by county levies, recruits and garrisons held in strategic towns, but every suppression consumed a batch of usable soldiers and a sum of collectable revenue, and a new rebellion always surfaced in some other county. The collapse of the Sui was therefore not decided by any single battle; it was exhausted by this constantly repeated cycle. Three years later, in the thirteenth year of Daye (617), the Taiyuan garrison commander Li Yuan rose in arms; a year after that the emperor was killed at Jiangdu and the Sui fell. The local order that the Tang took over was reassembled out of the pieces which these risings had already broken apart.
